ev.q: Women (24.4%) had a significantly higher prevalence of disability compared with men (19.1%) at all ages.
the prevalence of disability in 2005 (21.8%) remained unchanged from 1999 (22.0%)
the prevalence of self-reported disabilities among civilian noninstitutionalized U.S. adults aged ≥18 years was 21.8%
the estimated absolute number of persons reporting a disability increased 7.7%, from 44.1 to 47.5 million
the total estimated population reporting a disability was 47.5 million
the estimated population with a disability among persons aged 45--64 years (17.3 million) was not statistically different (p=0.081)
significantly higher among women (24.4%; CI = 23.7--25.1) compared with men (19.1%; CI = 18.5--19.7) overall and in all age groups
Data used for this report are cross-sectional findings from the Wave 5 disability topical module

methods_quotes.q: Differences in the prevalence of disability by sex across age groups and other comparisons were assessed by z-test
considered statistically significant if the 95% confidence interval (CI) of the difference excluded zero (p<0.05)
accounting for the complex survey design, and adjusting, in part, for undercoverage
All estimates in this report have been adjusted for sample size, clustering, survey design, and other features
Weighted estimates less than 200,000 are based on a small sample size and are likely unreliable
